_comment: Capability and delegation descriptions fed to Jev for subagent routing. Keys under families are AGY model IDs with the effort suffix (-low/-medium/-high) stripped. Models listed by `agy models` but missing here still get routed using the generic description. Edit freely.

delegation.delegate_subagent: Codebase search, reading/editing files, implementing features, fixing bugs, writing or running tests, debugging crashes/hooks, binary analysis, or code review.
delegation.handle_directly: Direct chat reply to a simple user question that requires no code or file work, OR Steam Deck hardware deployment (deck-ctl.sh, steamos-ctl.sh) and release publishing (./install.sh release, git push).

families.gemini-4-argon: Flagship Gemini. Strongest at deep multi-step reasoning, very large context analysis, architecture/design decisions and hard research synthesis. Slow and expensive.
families.gemini-3.8-flash: Fast, cheap Gemini. Good for codebase search and discovery, reading/summarising files, simple mechanical edits, log triage and quick lookups. Weak on subtle bugs.
families.claude-opus-5-5: Top-tier Claude coding/agentic model. Best for complex multi-file C++ changes, memory hooking, reverse engineering, subtle debugging and security review. Slow and expensive.
families.claude-sonnet-5-5: Balanced Claude coding model. Good for standard feature implementation, writing tests, shell/Python scripts, refactors of moderate size and code review.
families.gpt-oss-120b: Open-weight GPT model (medium effort only). Suitable for low-stakes bulk text work, simple classification-style subtasks or a cheap independent second opinion.

efforts.low: Trivial or well-specified subtask; little reasoning needed (lookups, renames, formatting, listing files).
efforts.medium: Normal engineering subtask with some ambiguity (implement a feature, fix a known bug, write tests).
efforts.high: Hard, high-stakes or open-ended subtask (crash/race debugging, binary analysis, design, security-sensitive changes).
